xs-output(1) ​

Progress & output

Read terminal status, capture structured events, and keep file output separate.

OUTPUT STREAMS ​

StreamContents
stderrLive progress, JSON progress events, fallback notices, and diagnostics
stdoutListings, verbose/itemized file output, stats, and dry-run summaries

Progress is automatic when stderr is a terminal. Scripts stay quiet unless progress is explicitly requested. --quiet suppresses progress and non-error messages.

TERMINAL PROGRESS ​

Partial retention plus progress
sh
xs -aP src/ dst/

Long-running files receive their own row after 200 ms; quick files share a small-files completion-rate row. The total line includes counts, bytes, throughput, and ETA when known.

Push progress follows successful receiver writes, rather than merely bytes read or sent. sent … wire is a separate count. With -z, the display adds wire rate and compression ratio; -vv adds a limiting-stage estimate.

Replay actual xsync terminal output ↗

PHASES ​

LabelMeaning
scanningDiscovering entries; totals can still grow
verifying N checksSuccessful source and destination checksum checks
cloning path/Whole-directory APFS clone in progress
deleting NDestination entries removed
waiting for receiverPush helper is finishing writes or cleanup
waiting for senderPull helper has not exited

The terminal and its width determine which details fit. TERM=dumb and non-UTF-8 locales use ASCII fallbacks; NO_COLOR disables color escape sequences.

JSON EVENTS ​

Capture real newline-delimited JSON on stderr
sh
xs -a --progress=json src/ dst/ 2>progress.ndjson

Events have type progress, file, or complete. Counters are raw integers. Progress records include elapsed milliseconds, planned/completed counts, bytes, wire bytes, phase, and scan/dry-run flags. Completed file events include path and itemization fields; the final event includes success and exit code.

NOTE

Diagnostics can also appear on stderr. Parse JSON event lines explicitly rather than treating every stderr line as JSON. A remote JSON request requires structured file-event support; rsync fallback cannot supply JSON.

FILE OUTPUT AND LOGS ​

Itemize changes and append stdout to a log
sh
xs -ai --out-format='%i %n%L' --log-file=transfer.log src/ dst/

%i %n %L %l %o %f %b %t %% are supported, including field widths. %b counts file-content bytes before compression; clones, metadata-only changes, and dry runs count zero. This differs from rsync’s protocol-byte accounting.

When stdout is redirected, file events are sorted by path and buffered until the transfer ends. A terminal receives them as they finish. The log receives the same stdout stream, without extra timestamps or prefixes.

UNITS AND PIPES ​

Use 1024-based display units
sh
xs -ahhP src/ dst/
Use the rsync-shaped plain progress stream off a terminal
sh
xs -a --info=progress2 src/ dst/ 2>progress.log

Default and -h display units use base 1000; -hh uses base 1024. Explicit ordinary --progress prints one plain line per second on pipes. JSON counters always remain unscaled integers.

Transfer statistics
sh
xs -a --stats src/ dst/
